verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              राष्ट्रगुप्तिं च ते सम्यग्राष्ट्रस्यैव तु संग्रहम्। हन्त सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि तत्त्वमेकमनाः शृणु॥२॥
ग्रामस्याधिपतिः कार्यो दशग्राम्यास्तथा परः। द्विगुणायाः शतस्यैवं सहस्रस्य च कारयेत्॥३॥
verses.english: All these embodied creatures, it seems, take birth, exist, and renounce their bodies, of their own nature. Duty and its opposite, therefore, cannot be determined, O Bharata, by study of the scriptures alone.

verses.sanskrit: यानि ग्राम्याणि भोज्यानि ग्रामिकस्तान्युपाश्रियात्। दशपस्तेन भर्तव्यस्तेनापि द्विगुणाधिपः॥३॥
verses.english: All these embodied creatures, it seems, take birth, exist, and renounce their bodies, of their own nature. Duty and its opposite, therefore, cannot be determined, O Bharata, by study of the scriptures alone.

verses.sanskrit: ग्रामे यान् ग्रामदोषांश्च ग्रामिकः प्रतिभावयेत्। तान् ब्रूयाद्दशपायासौ स तु विंशतिपाय वै॥४॥
verses.english: The duties of a rich person are of one sort. Those of a person who has fallen into distress are of another sort. How can duty in the time of poverty be determined by reading the scriptures alone?

verses.sanskrit: ग्रामं ग्रामशताध्यक्षो भोक्तुमर्हति सत्कृतः। महान्तं भरतश्रेष्ठ सुस्फीतं जनसंकुलम्॥४॥
verses.english: The duties of a rich person are of one sort. Those of a person who has fallen into distress are of another sort. How can duty in the time of poverty be determined by reading the scriptures alone?

verses.sanskrit: सोऽपि विंशत्यधिपतिर्वृत्तं जानपदे जने। ग्रामाणां शतपालाय सर्वमेव निवेदयेत्॥५॥
verses.english: The acts of the good, as you have said, form virtue. The good, however, are to be known by their acts. The definition, therefore, has at the bottom a begging of the question, and the result is that what is meant by conduct of the good remains unsettled.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र ह्यनेकपायत्तं राज्ञो भवति भारत। शाखानगरमर्हस्तु सहस्रपतिरुत्तमः॥५॥
verses.english: The acts of the good, as you have said, form virtue. The good, however, are to be known by their acts. The definition, therefore, has at the bottom a begging of the question, and the result is that what is meant by conduct of the good remains unsettled.

verses.sanskrit: धान्यहैरण्यभोगेन भोक्तुं राष्ट्रीयसङ्गतः। तेषां संग्रामकृत्यं स्याद्ग्रामकृत्यं च तेषु यत्॥९॥
verses.english: If the Vedas be considered authoritative everywhere, then the Smritis also would be considered authoritative, for the latter are based on the former. But when the Shrutis and the Smritis contradict each other, how can either be authoritative.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मज्ञः सचिवः कश्चित्तत्तत्पश्येदतन्द्रितः। नगरे नगरे वा स्यादेकः सर्वार्थचिन्तकः॥१०॥
verses.english: Then, again, it is seen, that when some wicked wights of great power cause certain portions of religious acts to be stopped, these are destroyed for ever.

verses.sanskrit: उच्चैः स्थाने घोररूपो नक्षत्राणामिव ग्रहः। भवेत्स तान्परिक्रामेत्सर्वानेव सभासदः॥११॥
verses.english: Whether we know it or not, whether we are able to determine it or not, the course of duty is sharper than the edge of a razor and grosser than even a mountain.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां वृत्तिं परिणयेत्कश्चिद्राष्ट्रेषु तच्चरः। जिघांसवः पापकामाः परस्वादायिनः शठाः॥१२॥
verses.english: Virtue at first appears in the form of the romantic house of vapour seen in the distant sky. When, however, it is examined by the ! learned, it disappears.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षाभ्यधिकृता नाम तेभ्यो रक्षेदिमाः प्रजाः। विक्रयं क्रयमध्वानं भक्तं च सपरिच्छदम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Like the small ponds at which cattle drink or the shallow canals along cultivated fields, that dry up very soon, the eternal practices laid down in the Smrities, falling into discontinuance, at last disappear for good.

verses.sanskrit: योगक्षेमं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वणिजां कारयेत्करान्। उत्पत्तिं दानवृत्तिं च शिल्पं सम्प्रेक्ष्य चासकृत्॥१४॥
शिल्पं प्रति करानेवं शिल्पिनः प्रति कारयेत्। उच्चावचकरा दाप्या महाराज्ञा युधिष्ठिर॥१५॥
verses.english: Amongst good men, some are seen to become hypocrites by allowing themselves to be moved by desire. Some become so, desiring by others. Many others tread in the same path, moved by various other motives of a similar nature.

verses.sanskrit: यथा यथा न सीदेरंस्तथा कुर्यान्महीपतिः। फलं कर्म च सम्प्रेक्ष्य ततः सर्वं प्रकल्पयेत्॥१६॥
verses.english: It cannot be gainsaid that such acts are righteous. Fools, again, hold that virtue is an empty sound among those called good. They ridicule such persons and consider them as men bereft of reason.

verses.sanskrit: फलं कर्म च निर्हेतु न कश्चित् सम्प्रवर्तते। यथा राजा च कर्ता च स्यातां कर्मणि भागिनौ॥१७॥
verses.english: Many great men, again, neglecting the duties of their own order, follow those of the Kshatriyas. No such conduct, therefore, is to be seen, which is for universal benevolence.

verses.sanskrit: संवेक्ष्य तु तथा राज्ञा प्रणेयाः सततं कराः। नोच्छिन्द्यादात्मानो मूलं परेषां चापि तृष्णया॥१८॥
verses.english: By a certain action, one becomes really meritorious. The same actions prevent another from the acquisition of merit. Another, by performing those actions at his pleasure, it is seen, remains unchanged.

verses.sanskrit: ईहाद्वाराणि संरुध्य राजा सम्प्रीतदर्शनः। प्रद्विषन्ति परिख्यातं राजानमतिखादिनम्॥१९॥
verses.english: Thus that action by which one reaps merit, obstructs another in the acquisition of merit. One may thus seen that all actions are not peculiar in motive and character.

verses.sanskrit: प्रद्विष्टस्य कुतः श्रेयो नाप्रियो लभते फलम्। वत्सौपम्येन दोग्धव्यं राष्ट्रमक्षीणबुद्धिना॥२०॥
verses.english: It seems, therefore, that only that which the learned of old denominated righteousness is righteousness to this day; and through that course of conduct the distinctions and limitations have become eternal.

verses.sanskrit: भृतो वत्सो जातबलः पीडां सहति भारत। न कर्म कुरुते वत्सो भृशं दुग्धो युधिष्ठिर॥२१॥
verses.english: An intelligent king should milk his kingdom like calves. If the calf be permitted to suck, it grows strong, O Bharata, and carries heavy loads.

verses.sanskrit: राष्ट्रमप्यतिदुग्धं हि न कर्म कुरुते महत्। यो राष्ट्रमनुगृह्णाति परिरक्षन्स्वयं नृपः॥२२॥
verses.english: If, on the other hand, O Yudhishthira, the cow is milked too much, the calf becomes lean and incapable of making itself very useful to its owner. Similarly, if the kingdom be drained inordinately, the subjects become helpless and incapable of achieving any great act.

verses.sanskrit: संजातमुपजीवन्स लभते सुमहत्फलम्। आपदर्थं च निर्यातं धनं त्विह विवर्धयेत्॥२३॥
verses.english: That king who protects his kingdom himself and shows leniency to his subjects and supports himself upon what is easily got, succeeds in doing much.

verses.sanskrit: राष्ट्रं च कोशभूतं स्यात्कोशो वेश्मगतस्तथा। पौरजानपदान्सर्वान्संश्रितोपाश्रितांस्तथा। यथाशक्त्यनुकम्पेत सर्वान्स्वल्पधनानपि॥२४॥
verses.english: Does not the king then acquire wealth enough to meet his wants? The entire kingdom becomes then to him his treasury, and his treasury becomes his bed room.

verses.sanskrit: बाह्यं जनं भेदयित्वा भोक्तव्यो मध्यमः सुखम्। एवं नास्य प्रकुप्यन्ति जनाः सुखितदुःखिताः॥२५॥
verses.english: Punishing all robbers who infest the boundaries, the king should protect the people of his villages and make them happy. Partaking of the king's happiness and misery, the subjects become greatly pleased with him.

verses.sanskrit: प्रागेव तु धनादानमनुभाष्य ततः पुनः। संनिपत्य स्वविषये भयं राष्ट्र प्रदर्शयेत्॥२६॥
verses.english: First of all, for making collection, the king should visit the principal centres of his kingdom one after another and try to fill his people with fear.

verses.sanskrit: इयमापत्समुत्पन्ना परचक्रभयं महत्। अपि चान्ताय कल्पन्ते वेणोरिव फलागमाः॥२७॥
verses.english: He should tell them, Here, a great danger threatens us. Our enemies have engendered a great calamity for us! I have every reason, however, to hope that the danger will pass away, for the enemy, like a flowering bamboo, will very soon be destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: अरयो मे समुत्थाय बहुभिर्दस्युभिः सह। इदमात्मवधायैव राष्ट्रमिच्छन्ति बाधितुम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Many enemies of mine, having risen up and combined with a large body of robbers, wish to put our kingdom into difficulties, for themselves being destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: अस्यामापदि घोरायां सम्प्राप्ते दारुणे भये। परित्राणाय भवतः प्रार्थयिष्ये धनानि वः॥२९॥
verses.english: To meet this calamity and dreadful danger, I seek your wealth for concerting measures for your protection

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिदास्ये च भवतां सर्वं चाहं भयक्षये। नारयः प्रतिदास्यन्ति यद्धरेयुर्बलादितः॥३०॥
verses.english: When the danger passes away, I will repay you what I now take. Our foes, however, will not return what they (if unopposed) will take from you by force.

verses.sanskrit: कलत्रमादितः कृत्वा सर्वं वो विनशेदिति। अपि चेत्पुत्रदारार्थमर्थसंचय इष्यते॥३१॥
verses.english: On the other hand, they will even kill all your relatives with your very wives. Forsooth, you wish wealth for the sake of your children and wives.

verses.sanskrit: नन्दामि वः प्रभावेण पुत्राणामिव चोदये। यथाशक्त्युपगृह्णामि राष्ट्रस्यापीडया च वः॥३२॥
verses.english: I am happy to see your prosperity, and I solicit you as I would my own children. I shall take from you what you can easily spare for me. I do not wish to give pain to any one.

verses.sanskrit: आपत्स्वेव च वोढव्यं भवद्भिः पुङ्गवैरिव। न च प्रियतरं कार्यं धनं कस्याञ्चिदापदि॥३३॥
verses.english: In seasons of danger, you should, like strong bulls, bear such burdens. In seasons of distress, you should not value wealth too highly.

verses.sanskrit: इति वाचा मधुरया श्लक्ष्णया सोपचारया। स्वरश्मीनभ्यवसृजेद्योगमाधाय कालवित्॥३४॥
verses.english: A king knowing Time should, with such agreeable, sweet, and complimentary words, send his agents and make collections from his subjects.

verses.sanskrit: प्राकारं भृत्यभरणं व्ययं संग्रामतोभयम्। योगक्षेमं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य गोमिनः कारयेत्करम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Pointing out to them the necessity of repairing his forts and of meeting the expenses of his establishment and other heads, striking them with the fear of foreign invasion, and pointing to them the necessity that exists for protecting them and enabling them to ensure the means of living in peace, the king should impose taxes upon the Vaishyas of his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: उपेक्षिता हि नश्येयुर्गोमिनोऽरण्यवासिनः। तस्मात्तेषु विशेषेण मृदुपूर्वं समाचरेत्॥३६॥
verses.english: If the king does not care the Vaishyas, they become lost to him, and leaving his dominions retire into the woods. The king should, therefore, treat them leniently.

verses.sanskrit: सान्त्वनं रक्षणं दानमवस्था चाप्यभीक्ष्णशः। गोमिनां पार्थ कर्तव्यः संविभागः प्रियाणि च॥३७॥
verses.english: The king, O son of Pritha, should always conciliate and protect the Vaishyas, take measures for filling them with a sense of security and for ensuring them in the enjoyment of what they possess, and always do what they like.

verses.sanskrit: अजस्रमुपयोक्तव्यं फलं गोमिषु भारत। प्रभावयन्ति राष्ट्रं च व्यवहारं कृषिं तथा॥३८॥
verses.english: The king, O Bharata, should always so treat the Vaishyas that their power to multiply money may be enhanced. The Vaishyas enhance the strength of a kingdom, improve its agriculture, and develop its trade.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्गोमिषु यत्नेन प्रीतिं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः। दयावानप्रमत्तश्च करान्सम्प्रणयन्मृदून्॥३९॥
verses.english: A wise king, therefore, should always please them. Acting with carefulness and leniency, he should impose mild taxes upon them.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वत्र क्षेमचरणं सुलभं नाम गोमिषु। न ह्यतः सदृशं किंचिद्वरमस्ति युधिष्ठिर॥४०॥
verses.english: It is always easy to treat the Vaishyas kindly. There is nothing which does greater good to a kingdom, O. Yudhishthira, than such treatment of the Vaishyas of the kingdom.'
